variants.title: Climb the evidence ladder
variants.context: A score change proves the measurement moved, not why. The evidence ladder holds one source of change still while another moves: frozen judges isolate the application, stable anchors expose the judge, and matched slices separate traffic mix from behavior.
variants.prompt: A weekly score falls six points and the team is ready to revert the prompt. Put the attribution steps in order.

items.text: Score baseline and candidate outputs with one frozen judge to isolate application behavior.
Note the top-line delta, which establishes that the measurement changed and nothing more.
Reweight or match the traffic slices, and read the gap between raw and matched results as the mix effect.
Replay identical stored outputs through both judges, since movement on stable anchors is evaluator drift.
Inspect versioned traces to locate the first changed component on the failing path.

variants.hint: Which comparison sends the same outputs through two different judges?
variants.explanation: Each rung holds one source of change still, so the effects can be separated instead of guessed at.

variants.title: Climb the evidence ladder
variants.context: A score change proves the measurement moved, not why. The evidence ladder holds one source of change still while another moves: frozen judges isolate the application, stable anchors expose the judge, and matched slices separate traffic mix from behavior.
variants.prompt: A judge model was auto-upgraded by the provider in the same week that a retrieval index shipped. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Score the old and new index outputs with the old judge only, so the retrieval change stands on its own.
Record the size of the observed movement before assigning it to either change.
Walk the versioned traces of failing requests to name the first component that differs.
Send last month's stored outputs through the old and new judges to measure how much the judge alone moved.
Match the cohorts on language and intent to remove any traffic shift from the comparison.

variants.hint: Two changes shipped together, so each needs a comparison that holds the other still.
variants.explanation: Stable anchors measure judge movement, and a frozen judge measures application movement. Neither answer comes from the top-line number.

variants.title: Climb the evidence ladder
variants.context: A score change proves the measurement moved, not why. The evidence ladder holds one source of change still while another moves: frozen judges isolate the application, stable anchors expose the judge, and matched slices separate traffic mix from behavior.
variants.prompt: Support quality drops after a campaign brings a new customer segment, and no release shipped that week. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Reweight the slices to last month's traffic mix and compare the matched result with the raw one.
Open the traces for the new segment to see which component the new requests actually stress.
Replay stable anchor outputs through the current judge to rule out an evaluator change.
Confirm the size of the blended drop as the starting observation.
Compare last month's and this month's outputs under one frozen judge on comparable cases.

variants.hint: A blended average moves when the mix moves, even if nothing else does.
variants.explanation: The difference between raw and matched results estimates the population effect, which no code change would explain.

variants.title: Turn drift into a bounded action
variants.context: Drift checks are release gates, not dashboards. Declare the change, run stable evidence, sample production, inspect slices and bounds, cap exposure, then refresh the suite without erasing history.
variants.prompt: A candidate application and a new judge rubric are both ready for the same release. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Continue, pause, or roll back with an owner, an abort threshold, and a tested recovery target.
Run deterministic checks, frozen golden sets, hidden holdouts, and paired judge anchors.
Compare raw counts, uncertainty, and critical cohorts before reading the aggregate.
Collect representative and risk-weighted production traces with known selection rules.
Promote confirmed production failures into a new regression version while keeping a hidden holdout.
Record the candidate application and evaluator identities, the affected claims, and the last known-good state.

variants.hint: The aggregate is read after the slices, not before them.
variants.explanation: Versioning both the application and the evaluator up front is what makes the later comparison interpretable.

variants.title: Turn drift into a bounded action
variants.context: Drift checks are release gates, not dashboards. Declare the change, run stable evidence, sample production, inspect slices and bounds, cap exposure, then refresh the suite without erasing history.
variants.prompt: A critical billing slice has a lower confidence bound under its release floor while the global score improves. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Run the frozen golden set and the hidden holdout against the candidate for that cohort.
Add the confirmed billing failures to a new suite version without touching the release holdout.
Name the billing slice as a protected cohort and record the last known-good release for it.
Read the billing counts and the lower bound rather than the improved global average.
Sample production billing traces with a risk weight so the cohort is not left underrepresented.
Cap exposure on the billing route and name the owner and the rollback target.

variants.hint: Which number is the gate written on when a cohort is protected?
variants.explanation: A global improvement cannot cancel a critical cohort whose lower bound sits under its floor.

variants.title: Turn drift into a bounded action
variants.context: Drift checks are release gates, not dashboards. Declare the change, run stable evidence, sample production, inspect slices and bounds, cap exposure, then refresh the suite without erasing history.
variants.prompt: A rare language slice has only nine sampled cases and the team wants to ship anyway. Put the steps in order.

items.text: Run the stable golden and holdout cases that exist for that language against the candidate.
Declare the language as a protected claim with its own floor and known-good baseline.
Increase the sampling weight for that language so its production evidence can grow.
Cap exposure for that language while the evidence is still thin, rather than approving on silence.
Fold the newly collected cases into a fresh suite version once they are validated.
Report the wide uncertainty on nine cases instead of reading its point estimate as a result.

variants.hint: Sparse evidence is not the same as evidence of safety.
variants.explanation: Detection readiness is assessed beside impact, so sparse evidence should cap exposure rather than quietly become approval.

variants.title: Split the delta into effects
variants.context: Paired comparisons split an observed delta into an application effect, a judge effect, and a population effect. Whatever those three do not explain is the residual, which is a signal that something is still unaccounted for.
variants.prompt: The same stored anchor outputs score 90.0 under the frozen judge and 84.0 under the current judge. How many points of the movement does the judge account for?
variants.hint: The outputs did not change between these two numbers.
variants.explanation: Movement on stable anchors is evaluator drift, because the only thing that changed between the two scores is the judge.

mistakes.feedback: You added the two anchor scores instead of comparing them.
That is the observed top-line delta, which still mixes all three sources.

variants.title: Split the delta into effects
variants.context: Paired comparisons split an observed delta into an application effect, a judge effect, and a population effect. Whatever those three do not explain is the residual, which is a signal that something is still unaccounted for.
variants.prompt: Under one frozen judge, the baseline outputs score 88.0 and the candidate outputs score 87.5 on the same cases. How many points of the movement does application behavior account for?
variants.hint: One judge, one case set, two versions of the product.
variants.explanation: A paired comparison under a frozen judge isolates application behavior, which is why the judge must not change during it.

mistakes.feedback: That is the judge effect, which is measured on stable anchors instead.
That is the observed delta, not the paired application effect.

variants.title: Split the delta into effects
variants.context: Paired comparisons split an observed delta into an application effect, a judge effect, and a population effect. Whatever those three do not explain is the residual, which is a signal that something is still unaccounted for.
variants.prompt: The observed delta is 8.0 points down. Application behavior explains 0.5 points down, the judge explains 6.0 points down, and the traffic mix explains 1.5 points down. How many points remain unexplained?
variants.hint: Add what the three effects account for before comparing it with what was observed.
variants.explanation: A residual near zero means the three paired comparisons account for the movement. A large residual means something is still unmeasured.

mistakes.feedback: You left the population effect out of the explained total.
That is the observed delta before the explained effects are subtracted.

variants.title: Name what actually changed
variants.context: The same drop can mean the system changed, the evaluator changed, the population changed, or the instrumentation changed. Treating every movement as model drift sends the team toward the wrong fix.
variants.prompt: Quality drops five points the morning after a telemetry release. Replaying the same sampled outputs through the same judge reproduces last week's scores exactly.
options: Roll back the model, since the drop began within a day of the release window.
Check event definitions, missing joins, delays, and duplicated records before changing the product.
Recalibrate the judge, since the scores it now reports disagree with the dashboard.
optionFeedback: Nothing here points at the model, and the replay already shows the outputs score the same.
Identical outputs scoring identically means the evidence changed before scoring, which is instrumentation.
The judge reproduced last week's scores, so the evaluator is the one component shown to be stable.
variants.hint: The replay held the outputs and the judge constant. What is left?
variants.explanation: Sampling, event definitions, missing joins, and duplicated records change the evidence before scoring begins.

variants.title: Name what actually changed
variants.context: The same drop can mean the system changed, the evaluator changed, the population changed, or the instrumentation changed. Treating every movement as model drift sends the team toward the wrong fix.
variants.prompt: Every language and intent slice holds its pass rate, but the blended score falls three points after a campaign brings a large new intent.
options: Report the matched or reweighted result and treat the drop as a change in traffic mix.
Roll back the prompt, since the blended score crossed its declared release floor.
Lower the floors to match the new blended baseline the campaign produced.
optionFeedback: Stable within-slice rates alongside a falling blend is the signature of a population change.
No slice regressed, so a rollback would remove a version that is behaving exactly as before.
Moving the floor to fit the new number abandons the claim the floor existed to protect.
variants.hint: Every slice held. What else can move an average?
variants.explanation: Population change shifts the mix of intents, languages, and difficulty even when within-slice behavior is stable.

variants.title: Name what actually changed
variants.context: The same drop can mean the system changed, the evaluator changed, the population changed, or the instrumentation changed. Treating every movement as model drift sends the team toward the wrong fix.
variants.prompt: A provider upgrades the judge model. Stable anchor outputs now score four points lower, while candidate and baseline outputs are byte for byte unchanged.
options: Adopt the new scores as more accurate, since the newer judge model is the stronger one.
Recalibrate on the anchors and keep the old judge available for paired replay.
Treat it as a product regression and roll back to the previous application revision.
optionFeedback: A newer judge is a different measuring instrument, and calling it more accurate is an untested claim.
Anchor movement is judge drift, so the fix is recalibration with the old judge preserved for comparison.
The application outputs did not change, so there is no product behavior for a rollback to fix.
variants.hint: The outputs are identical. What does that leave as the only moving part?
variants.explanation: Judge drift imitates product drift, so anchors are replayed through both judges before anyone edits the application.

variants.title: Sort the five stores
variants.context: Five stores stay independently versioned: golden and holdout sets, production samples, evaluation runs, change ledgers, and decision logs. Continuous evaluation is a join across them, not a query over anonymous scores.
variants.prompt: A drift investigation needs five kinds of record. Match each store to what it preserves.

pairs.label: Golden and holdout sets
pairs.detail: Stable claims, hidden release evidence, rubrics, and risk labels.

pairs.label: Production samples
pairs.detail: Real cases, slice membership, selection probabilities, and retention constraints.

pairs.label: Evaluation runs
pairs.detail: Raw counts, scores, confidence bounds, judge outputs, disagreements, and errors.

pairs.label: Change ledgers
pairs.detail: Every behavior-changing application and evaluator version.

pairs.label: Decision logs
pairs.detail: Who shipped, paused, rolled back, or accepted an exception, and why.

variants.hint: Two of these hold cases, and the difference is where those cases came from.
variants.explanation: Independent versioning is what lets a team say whether the cases, the system, the scoring, or the decision changed.

variants.title: Sort the five stores
variants.context: Five stores stay independently versioned: golden and holdout sets, production samples, evaluation runs, change ledgers, and decision logs. Continuous evaluation is a join across them, not a query over anonymous scores.
variants.prompt: Five records are missing and the investigation has stalled. Match each missing record to the store that should hold it.

pairs.label: Golden and holdout sets
pairs.detail: The risk label that marks this case as release critical.

pairs.label: Production samples
pairs.detail: The probability with which this trace was selected for review.

pairs.label: Evaluation runs
pairs.detail: The confidence bound reported alongside the slice pass rate.

pairs.label: Change ledgers
pairs.detail: The date the judge prompt was last edited.

pairs.label: Decision logs
pairs.detail: The expiry attached to the approved exception.

variants.hint: A selection probability describes how a case was sampled, not how it scored.
variants.explanation: Selection probabilities are what allow an oversampled rare slice to be reweighted back into a fleet estimate.

variants.title: Sort the five stores
variants.context: Five stores stay independently versioned: golden and holdout sets, production samples, evaluation runs, change ledgers, and decision logs. Continuous evaluation is a join across them, not a query over anonymous scores.
variants.prompt: A reviewer asks five questions during a drift postmortem. Match each question to the store that answers it.

pairs.label: Golden and holdout sets
pairs.detail: Which cases were deliberately kept hidden from tuning?

pairs.label: Production samples
pairs.detail: Which tenants and risk classes did the sampled traffic cover?

pairs.label: Evaluation runs
pairs.detail: How wide was the interval on the failing slice?

pairs.label: Change ledgers
pairs.detail: Which retrieval version was live when the score moved?

pairs.label: Decision logs
pairs.detail: Who accepted the exception that kept the rollout going?

variants.hint: One of these questions is about accountability rather than measurement.
variants.explanation: Never interpret a score change until you can name what was tested, which system produced it, which population supplied it, and which evaluator judged it.
